competing_explanation: A genuine inconsistency among saved per-seed predictions, ensemble candidate scores and R5 policy rows is rejected by the full finite-population audit. Python float64 arithmetic averaging differs numerically from R5's authoritative Torch float32 reduction, but the prespecified sensitivity comparison shows zero action-assignment changes and zero top-39 membership changes across all four cells and both folds.
gate_reasons: All eight declared assets passed SHA-256 and lifecycle verification; the protected-data-free full-scale contract and all four workload milestones completed.
All 6,144 ensemble rows and all three score fields reproduce exactly under `torch.float32 -> stack -> mean(0)`, with zero native score mismatches.
All saved severe labels reproduce exactly under R5's any-operator group/action threshold semantics, with zero label mismatches.
All 3,072 saved policy rows replay exactly with maximum absolute field difference 0, and every four-cell count and operator gain matches the compact R5 cell summary.
The float64 sensitivity has 10,541 exact-value differences, maximum absolute difference 1.1920928955078125e-7, but zero action or top-39 changes.
limitations: R8 is an integrity audit, not an Action x Coverage x Risk mechanism result and not a restoration-model experiment.

PASS authorizes only review of a new independently identified attribution contract; it does not authorize automatic execution, training, inference, full OOF, confirmation, canary, locked test or deployment.

Any replacement attribution contract must consume saved authoritative candidate scores or reconstruct with exact R5 float32 semantics and must use R5's any-operator group/action severe-label definition.
R5, R6 and R7 terminal decisions remain unchanged and must remain separately archived.
primary_result: R8-A0 passes the complete score, label and policy identity audit: R5 raw artifacts are internally consistent under their authoritative float32 and any-operator semantics, and the R6/R7 input stops are explained by narrower audit reconstruction contracts rather than invalid R5 evidence.
